title: Service Marketing Examples: Successful Marketing Techniques
summary: Learn from how service brands have marketed their services using techniques like user-generated content, digital catalogs, events, and more.
body_markdown:
A service business is based on expertise, resources, and time, rather than physical products. The goal of service marketing is to convey service quality through positive customer experiences and satisfaction, proven expertise, and content or visuals that help your customers know what to expect.


There are many different ways to achieve that goal, purely because there are so many different service styles catering to unique audiences. The service industry is responsible for 73% of the US gross domestic product (GDP), worth an estimated[$22.7 trillion in 2026](https://www.stlouisfed.org/open-vault/2026/feb/how-important-is-the-services-sector-to-the-us-economy) , and encompasses everything from professional services like accounting and advertising to software engineering and sales, financial services and consultants, hotels and daycare centers.


In this article, you’ll find examples of service marketing, along with effective service marketing strategies to incorporate into your own approach.


## What is service marketing?


[Service marketing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/service-marketing) focuses on the promotion of a service business that sells an intangible good or activity, as opposed to product marketing, which centers on a physical product. A successful service marketing strategy communicates the value of an experience that has not happened yet, creates demand for that experience, and builds trust with potential customers across digital platforms like websites, social media, and review sites.

Here are successful digital marketing examples from companies across the service industry spectrum:


### Bashify


Using social media platforms to showcase the service experience helps potential customers know what to expect from your services—and helps you highlight the value of what you provide. Event décor brand[Bashify’s](https://bashify.co/) social media marketing strategy emphasizes aspects such as price transparency, installation construction, and a do-it-yourself approach to event décor with tutorials and kits to help demystify the process.


“People want to buy things from people,” Founder Bre Giglio says on an episode of the[Shopify Masters podcast](https://www.shopify.com/blog/bashify-from-side-hustle-to-six-figures) . “I really try to bring customers and viewers through the experience, because it helps them see that there’s a person behind this.”


Bre explains that she operates two accounts to cover distinct segments of their audience: a main account for[Bashify](https://www.instagram.com/bashify.co/?hl=en) , and her[personal account](https://www.instagram.com/bre.giglio) , where she shares commentary and behind-the-scenes clips from the business. “When I post on Bashify, it’s more of a buttoned-up catalog of our work. If you come to my page, that’s where there’s more opinion, more personality, a little bit more spunk.”


### Chillhouse SOHO


[Chillhouse](https://chillhouse.com/) began as an ecommerce skin and nail care brand specializing in products, specifically, press-on nails and polishes. In 2019, it expanded to include a spa, café, and event space at[Chillhouse SOHO](https://chillhousesoho.com/) .


*Source:[Chillhouse SOHO](https://chillhousesoho.com/pages/lookbook)*


Their service marketing strategy includes a visually compelling manicure services[lookbook](https://chillhousesoho.com/pages/lookbook) in the style of a product portfolio, which gives customers an anticipatory experience of the service, the breadth of options, as well as a sense of staff expertise, execution, and quality outcomes they should expect. In contrast, their[massage and facial services](https://chillhousesoho.com/pages/spa-services) marketing (harder to visualize with an outcome) favor an aspirational vibe, with images of models looking calm and refreshed.


### Otherhalf Studio


[Testimonials](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-testimonials) and[social proof](https://www.shopify.com/blog/social-proof) are critical pieces of service marketing: Since a service cannot be tested or handled before purchase, customer reviews play a major role in convincing others to sign on.


Design-first agency[Otherhalf Studio](https://otherhalf.studio/) relies on both social proof and quantifiable improvements to demonstrate expertise and build trust. “Sales, especially in the world of high-ticket services, is all about relationship-building. Lots of decisions come down to emotions. Do I trust this person? Do I like them? Do I actually believe that they can deliver?” Cofounder Jamil Bhuya says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/otherhalf-studio-designing-successfully)* .


*Source:[Otherhalf Studio](https://otherhalf.studio/)*


Otherhalf Studio’s homepage shows a banner with rotating key stats, emphasizing referrals and quality-at-speed. At a glance, it does three things: captures the spirit of the business (built on referrals), shows the reader what to expect from the mechanics of the service itself (timeline, average review rounds), and crucially, emphasises the service value (approval rate).


It’s followed by a brand statement that underscores the same themes: the quality of the community, speed, and taste.


### Telescope Studio


[Telescope Studio](https://www.telescopestudio.com/) helps brands create merchandise and custom gifts—providing a “strategic approach” from ideation to delivery.


The brand creates digital catalogs to help prospective customers learn about their offerings. These catalogs combine mood boards, creative briefs, newsletters, and product catalogs. They also include client testimonials (a case study from Maven) with examples from a broader content marketing strategy (an interview with garden writer Monty Don, for example).


*Source:[Telescope Studio](https://www.telescopestudio.com/from-the-garden)*


“We’re really trying to gear people toward better choices in general, by helping them think critically about why they’re choosing a product and what they’re doing with design,” Founder Chloe Sapienza says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/telescope-corporate-gifting)* . “There are a lot of variables: there’s the budget, the existing branding guidelines, timeline, preferences, and a desire for everything to be uniformly liked—because you’re giving to a group, and not to an individual.”


*Source:[Telescope Studio](https://www.telescopestudio.com/from-the-garden)*


Not only does an editorial-style catalog make problem-solving within those guidelines more of a fun creative exercise for teams, it also helps create a cohesive experience. “It’s about giving people unique and inspiring ideas that they maybe hadn’t thought of, and finding new ways to showcase their idea on a product, with a bit of your influence in it as well,” she says. “I get a lot of joy out of knowing that we’re helping to bring smaller brands and local manufacturers into the fold of this world.”


### Salty Paws


A pet can’t tell you what they thought of a service their owners booked, but the[right visuals](https://www.shopify.com/blog/visual-marketing) can: for dog lovers, there is perhaps no stronger pitch than dog daycare center[Salty Paws](https://www.saltypawsnh.com/) ’ homepage line-up of good boys and girls on a perfect New Hampshire beach day.


*Source:[Salty Paws](https://www.saltypawsnh.com/)*


The image shows one of the business’s services in action (an outdoor pack adventure), demonstrates the owner’s ability to teach the dogs to follow commands (they’re off-leash and staying in place), and taps the emotionally driven decision-making process of their target audience, communicating value and trust.


## How to build a service marketing strategy


1. Focus on quality outcomes
2. Highlight your expertise
3. Make it easy to capture leads
4. Personalize messaging
5. Use UGC for social proof
6. Connect with your audience at events
7. Offer resources and digital products


“In the recruiting business, I view service marketing as a two-sided sell,” says Alston Chiang, CEO and founding partner of recruiting firm[Acacia](https://acaciarecruits.com/) . “You have to market the business, and the individual person giving the service; then you have to sell to the client, and the candidate.”


Service marketing means selling something a customer can’t touch or test out for themselves prior to purchase. Instead, you’ll need to speak to the individual touchpoints within the customer journey to bring it to life.


Here’s a step-by-step guide to building out a strategy:


### 1. Focus on quality outcomes


Because a customer won’t know if your service was a good decision until it’s done, one way to address their doubts is by showcasing quality results. That includes techniques like sharing case studies and client testimonials, before-and-after photos (for services like landscape projects, hair styling, or event decoration), and reposting social media content from satisfied customers on your own page or website.


It’s important to note that results are different from guarantees. “The hardest challenge with service marketing is the amount of variability in how the service can go,” Alston says. “No outcomes are guaranteed, because I can’t control if a candidate’s going to take a job, so we try to stay away from that in our marketing efforts.”


Instead of promising to fill a role in 30 days, for example, the firm keeps the focus on the client’s desired outcome—filling the role with quality talent—without introducing specifics that could set anyone up for disappointment.


Likewise, you might center your messaging on the solution you’ll have provided for customers by the end of the service. (For a daycare service, that might be peace of mind that your kids are safe and learning important skills while you’re at work.)


### 2. Highlight your expertise


Leading with you and your team’s hard-won expertise establishes credibility and helps to ease buyer skepticism or resistance. According to a recent report from[Insights Media](https://insights-media.kit.com/96c38a8e62) , 73% of decision-makers find thought leadership more trustworthy and compelling than traditional marketing materials.


In Acacia’s early days, marketing focused on its founder’s personal[reputation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/reputation-marketing) and experience to build trust. “That was a great way to say, ‘Hey, I’ve had this accolade; I hired an engineering team; We got acquired for a billion dollars; Do you want to work with me?’” Alston says.


Once the firm had established a strong track record of customer satisfaction, they shifted to a dual focus on a wider range of quality outcomes backed by deep industry expertise. “Everyone on my team has both internal recruiting experience and agency experience,” he says. “Startups love that because what that signals to them is that we know how to work at the pace of an agency recruiter, but we also know how to operationally set up the founder for success because we’ve all been either a head of talent or the first recruiter at a company.”


### 3. Make it easy to capture leads


To keep track of the audience you attract, use tools like[Shopify Forms](https://apps.shopify.com/shopify-forms) that help you build a robust contact list from site visitors, direct customer inquiries, and more. Customizable[appointment-booking apps](https://www.shopify.com/blog/appointment-booking-app) like[Cowlendar](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar) or[Apntly](https://apps.shopify.com/appointly) allow you to incorporate waivers, individual service providers, payment processing, and accepting deposits within a cohesive, branded portal.


### 4. Personalize messaging


In service marketing, where customers are both part of the service and its social proof, strong customer relationships are critical. Personalizing your messaging and marketing approach can help retain customers, encourage repeat business, and inspire word-of-mouth referrals.


According to an[Attentive study](https://www.attentive.com/blog/2026-personalization-trends) , 93% of shoppers are more likely to be loyal to a brand when it provides personalized experiences. For a service business, that means personalizing marketing efforts by[customer segment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-customer-segmentation) (like crafting specific messages over generic ones) and to[individual customers](https://www.shopify.com/blog/personalization-in-retail) (messaging that takes past preferences or purchases into account when providing recommendations, alerts, or in-store experiences).


Incorporating[customer relationship management (CRM)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/crm) software allows you to keep track of customer demographics, insights, and purchasing history so you can craft richer profiles—and marketing tailored to them.


### 5. Use UGC for social proof


[User-generated content (UGC)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/user-generated-content) is especially useful for service businesses looking to drive curiosity and brand trust: according to Emplifi’s[Q3 2025 Social Media Benchmarks report](https://emplifi.io/press/ugc-delivers-10x-higher-conversion-rates/) , social media posts featuring UGC drove over 10 times higher conversion rates than posts without it.


Capturing your service for social media creates eye-catching visuals, but partnering with content creators to do so generates valuable social proof. Use tools like[Shopify Collabs](https://apps.shopify.com/collabs) to build an affiliate program and connect with influencers and content creators whose style and reach complement yours.


### 6. Connect with your audience at events


Branded events are a low-pressure way for prospective clients and customers to interact with your business, while building personal connection and brand recognition. Acacia recently threw a Pride party to celebrate four years as a queer- and women-owned business, and they invited candidates who they were currently helping in their job search. Many brought a friend or fellow engineer along.


“One thing we’ve talked about was, maybe I need to get on TikTok, because that’s where the younger generation is,” Alston says. “But software engineers aren’t on TikTok. I like going to board game nights, you know? That’s where we meet people. That’s where we build the best relationships.” Identify where your target audience likes to spend time, and establish a presence where it makes the most sense.


### 7. Offer resources or digital products


Another way to build brand trust and goodwill with your audience is to offer free pieces of your insight or expertise in the form of informative blog posts or newsletters, guides, and tools like templates or tutorials.


Acacia recently launched a[Substack](https://eaganm.substack.com/p/the-acacia-accelerator) aimed at helping coach prospective applicants through the interview process—not their primary service as a recruiting business, but a key step in a successful outcome. “We’re building out more free resources for candidates who are on the job market,” Alston says. “We’re hoping that the Substack will help that information be more visible and easily distributable.”


Many service businesses also offer services in the form of digital products like consultations,[courses](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-create-an-online-course) , or memberships. Tools like Shopify’s[Digital Products app](https://apps.shopify.com/digital-downloads) make listing and checkout seamless.


## Service marketing examples FAQ


### What is service marketing?


Service marketing refers to strategies designed to promote service-based businesses (as opposed to product-driven ones). Because a service is essentially intangible until it is experienced, marketing requires an emphasis on expertise, outcomes, and customer reviews to communicate overall value.


### What are the seven Ps of service marketing?


The seven elements of a service marketing mix, also known as the seven Ps, are: product, price, place, promotion, people, processes, and physical evidence.


### What is an example of service marketing?


A graphic designer creating a portfolio of successful projects to promote their services is an example of service marketing. The portfolio may include reviews from satisfied customers and display statistics of relevant outcomes (increased conversion after a website redesign, for example).
